latest.title: Tencent AI chief warns of AI biology risks, SCMP reports - The Next Web
latest.summary: Tencent’s chief AI scientist has warned that AI models will soon be able to cause harm in biology, as they already can in cybersecurity. > “The cyber abilities of [AI] models and soon [the] bio abilit...
highlights: Tencent’s chief AI scientist has warned that AI models will soon be able to cause harm in biology, as they already can in cybersecurity. > “The cyber abilities of [AI] models and soon [the] bio ability of models will reach a threshold where it’s actually possible to do harm,” Yao said, according to the SCMP. He spoke days after Tencent launched Hy4, its new flagship model, on 4 November. In its launch announcement, Tencent said it left material on exploiting software flaws out of Hy4’s training data. Tencent also said that Hy4 has strong basic knowledge of biology, but is weaker than leading models at designing experiments. The company plans to release Hy4’s weights and a report on its safety testing in the coming days, Reuters reported. Hy4 ranks as the second-best Chinese model, according to benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis, the SCMP said. However, he argued that a mix of open and closed models may work best, because open models can also help defenders.

"We expect production and the delivery schedule ‌for contracted volumes to ⁠proceed without disruption," Ryu said, adding that the ministry was closely monitoring developments and discussing prices and schedules with ⁠Nvidia Korea. Nvidia's board said on Sunday it had opened an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a Chinese intelligence effort ​through his ​relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang. News of the controversy coincided with the cancellation of a visit to South Korea by Huang's daughter Madison Huang, an Nvidia senior director. South Korean AI startup Rebellions said her planned visit ‌to its headquarters and a partner dinner ​were cancelled because of unavoidable internal circumstances at ​Nvidia.
